mistake_reason: At step 9, WebSurfer proposed expanding the scope beyond the user’s original task—counting slides that mention crustaceans in the presentation—by including non-body cues (image alt-text, image filenames, speaker notes) and even suggesting the culinary umbrella term 'shellfish' as a proxy. This caused the team to drift from the core objective (textual slide mentions) into tangential signals and broadened criteria, ultimately inflating the count. This is a classic Task Derailment (FM-2.3): the agent redirected the analysis toward extraneous dimensions not requested, leading to an incorrect final answer.
